Development-only official C++ SDK scorecard probe without a package manager: the Dockerfile is both manifest and lock. Each ADD --checksum=sha256 line downloads one archive, and each record names its release tag as current, its GitHub repository, every archive URL with its SHA-256 and the license that the repository's license file states through the GitHub license API (CMake LICENSE.rst, nlohmann/json LICENSE.MIT, the others LICENSE). Both CMake 4.5.1 binary archives are one dependency because the build verifies both and unpacks the build architecture's. On 2026-11-15 every tag is its repository's GitHub latest release; the CMake and Abseil SHA-256 values equal the release API digests, and json.tar.xz and the generated google-cloud-cpp and opentelemetry-cpp tag archives, which have no published digest, were downloaded and hashed. The daily check fails when an ADD lacks --checksum or the Dockerfile and this record disagree on a URL, tag or SHA-256, and compares each tag with the repository's GitHub latest release; a latest release older than the pin, such as a patch for an older release line, fails the check instead of passing as CURRENT. opentelemetry-cpp contributes API headers only and CMake is a build tool. libcurl and OpenSSL come from the gcc image, whose index is pinned in docker.digests; the toolchain record names that image.
